customConcept.name: Olive Garden (Darden)
customConcept.blurb: Unlimited breadsticks, a 240-seat dining room and a menu built in a test kitchen in Orlando. You run the building; Darden runs everything else.

state.circumstances: You're the general manager of one Olive Garden. Darden owns the building, the brand, the menu and the money; you run the restaurant and are paid a base plus a bonus on profit.

setting.name: Retail corridor off the interstate
setting.desc: Across the parking lot from a big-box store and two blocks from the mall. Families, office lunches, church crowds after Sunday service, and a Saturday-night wait that runs out the door.

ev.text: Valentine's Day weekend: every booth booked, breadstick baskets going out by the hundred.
Mother's Day: the busiest Sunday of the year, a two-hour wait by noon.
Darden brings back Never Ending Pasta. Traffic jumps, the check drops, and the kitchen lives on the pasta cookers for weeks.
A new chain Italian place opened in the same shopping center, with an opening coupon in every mailbox.

desk.title: A church wants the back room every Sunday
desk.text: A large congregation nearby asks to book your private dining room for a 40-person lunch after services every Sunday, at a group price.

choices.label: Take the standing booking
choices.blurb: Steady money, and a slower Sunday for walk-ins.

log.text: You're the general manager of one Olive Garden. Darden owns the building, the brand, the menu and the money; you run the restaurant and are paid a base plus a bonus on profit.

world.notes: This is Olive Garden, the Italian-American chain owned by Darden Restaurants. Menus, recipes, national prices, suppliers and TV advertising come from Darden in Orlando; you can't rename dishes or swap the concept, but you run the floor, the kitchen, the staffing and local decisions. Unlimited soup, salad and breadsticks and the seasonal Never Ending Pasta promotion are central to the brand. Darden reported $5.6 million average annual sales per Olive Garden in fiscal 2025, a segment profit margin of about 22%, and company-wide food and beverage at about 30% and restaurant labour at about 32% of sales. Seat count, rent and this restaurant's exact sales are estimates for a typical suburban unit. Staff names are invented.

supplierPool.name: Darden distribution network
supplierPool.blurb: Darden buys centrally for every brand and ships through its distribution partners on a fixed schedule. You order from the system; you don't pick vendors.

menu.identity: Italian-American comfort at a price families can repeat every week: unlimited soup, salad and breadsticks, big pasta plates, a Tour of Italy.

team.name: Renee Castellano
team.bio: Managing partner: came up as a server at another Olive Garden and runs this one to Darden's playbook.

team.name: Luis Ferreira
team.bio: Culinary manager. Every sauce here comes from an Orlando recipe card, and he makes sure it tastes like it does in Ohio.

team.name: Tamika Brennan
team.bio: Kitchen manager who trains the line on the breadstick timer and the Never Ending Pasta rush.

profile.name: Darden Restaurants
profile.desc: The Orlando company that owns Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse and a dozen other brands. Olive Garden alone is around 935 restaurants and more than five billion dollars of sales a year.
profile.personality: Runs everything by the numbers and by the playbook. Menus, prices, marketing and suppliers are set in Orlando; a restaurant is judged on same-restaurant sales, guest scores and margin, and managers who keep all three green are left alone.

rep.name: Dana Whitfield
rep.title: Director of Operations
rep.style: Visits unannounced once a quarter, reads the scorecards before saying hello, and remembers every number you promised.

desk.title: Orlando wants a test
desk.text: Darden wants your restaurant to test a new menu item for eight weeks: new prep, new plating, a survey card on every table.

choices.label: Run the test properly
choices.blurb: Extra work, and you're noticed in Orlando.

choices.label: Run it by the book, no more

events.text: A regional audit team spent two days checking food-safety logs and cash handling against Darden's standards.

United States.name: United States

alcohol.note: Licensed by the state; quotas in some cities.

inspections.system: County or city health department inspections; letter grades posted in some cities.

United States.mealTimes: Lunch around noon to 1pm, dinner from about 6 to 8pm.
United States.customs: Guests expect fast, attentive service, free tap water and refills, and a check brought on request. Tipping 18-22% is expected at table service.
United States.labour: At-will employment in most states; overtime after 40 hours a week; minimum wages set by state and city.
